newsitem.title: USA: John Alden in pact with SunAmerica.
newsitem.headline: John Alden in pact with SunAmerica.

text.p: John Alden Financial Corp has entered into a definitive agreement to sell substantially all of its annuity business to SunAmerica Inc for about $240 million in cash.
The transaction is expected to be completed by the end of the first quarter of 1997 and is subject to regulatory approvals, John Alden and SunAmerica said.
John Alden said it expects to post a net deferred gain of about $45 million from the sale of its annuity business and the company's previously announced intention to sell its credit operations.
John Alden said the net deferred gain will be recognized as income as SunAmerica completes the assumption of policyholder liabilities.
John Alden said it expects to begin recognizing the gain in 1997 and to earn the majority of the gain in 1998.
SunAmerica chairman Eli Broad said he expects the acquisition to be accretive immediately.
"This transaction is in keeping with SunAmerica's strategy to enhance our dynamic internal growth with complementary acquisitions.
Broad said the acquisition will increase SunAmerica's annuity reserves to $21 billion from $16 billion, giving it greater critical mass and lowering its unit operating costs.

John Alden said its available capital will be enhanced by both the after-tax income generated from the transaction and by the release of the capital previously allocated to support the annuity business.

John Alden said it intends to use a portion of this available capital to strengthen its healthcare operations, after which it estimates there will be approximately $175 to $200 million of capital available for other uses.
This additional capital will be used primarily to repurchase common stock, to pay down debt and, to a lesser extent, for general corporate purposes, John Alden said.
"We made a decision earlier this year to focus the company's resources exclusively on our healthcare lines," said John Alden chairman Glendon E. Johnson.
The transaction with SunAmerica includes the sale of all of the common stock of John Alden Life Insurance Co of New York and the reinsurance of the annuity block of John Alden Life Insurance Co.
SunAmerica said the transaction will include a total of about $5.0 billion of annuity reserves.
The business consists of approximately 250,000 policies, a substantial portion of which are subject to surrender charges, making the block of business highly persistent, SunAmerica said.
The policies are almost entirely flexible- and single-premium fixed annuities sold through independent agents and financial institutions.

The related assets acquired primarily consist of high-quality, liquid investments, virtually all of which are rated investment grade, and a well-underwritten, seasoned portfolio of commercial and residential mortgage loans, SunAmerica said.

The total purchase price of about $240 million represents approximately $169 million paid to acquire the business and $71 million of adjusted capital and surplus in John Alden New York as of Sept 30, 1996, John Alden said.
It does not include any capital used to support the annuity business in John Alden Life Insurance Co.
